messages.author: c621ac38989fbf3c
messages.subject: speeding up model comparisons
parts:
Hi Paul,
 I've run a couple test models that I'd like to compare:

result ~ 1    vs
result ~ ( 1 | ID )

to see if the random term improves the model.

Result is binomial, n=36,000, and ID= 19,000 levels

The models like this (without all the smooth terms I've mentioned in my last post) run quickly enough using multi-core, but R crashes if I don't use pointwise comparison for WAIC or LOOIC. This is true even on the best computer I have available, which is an an 8 core / 3.5 GHz computer with 32 GB of RAM.

The pointwise WAIC comparison has taken around 12 hours and still isn't complete. Is this to be expected? Is there a way the pointwise comparison could be done with parallel processing to speed it up?

Thanks,
Paul

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] speeding up model comparisons
parts:
It could be made in parallel, but this likely had to be implemented in the loo package rather than in brms.

You could reduce the number of posterior samples involved in the comparisons, to make stuff fit into RAM by using the nsamples or subset argument of LOO.

messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] speeding up model comparisons
parts:
loo can be run in parallel using the "cores" argument. If you have enough RAM, you can set argument "pointwise" to FALSE, which will be way faster (but also memory consuming). So if "fit1" is your model, try

loo1 <- LOO(fit1, cores = <x>, pointwise = FALSE)
